title: Dock
summary: A workspace of panels (Toolbox | Canvas | Properties) laid out as a tree of resizable splits and tab groups. Drag a separator or use its arrow keys to resize, choose a tab to switch a group, and use a group's Move button to move its active panel to another group without a mouse. The arrangement is one JSON layout document you can read, store and set. Step 2 of #432: docked panels plus keyboard/menu move between groups; drag-to-dock, floating panels, collapse/rails and a pk-dock-panel element come in later steps.

props.name: layout
props.description: The arrangement: { version, seq, root } where root is a split { id, type: 'split', orientation, size, min, max, a, b } or a tab group { id, type: 'tabs', active, panels }. Leave it unset for the default arrangement derived from each panel's data-group. The element validates what it is given (panels that are not declared are dropped, panels the layout lacks are added, bad numbers are repaired). While the user resizes or chooses a tab the element owns it; after pk-layout-change the host does. Property or a JSON attribute.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of a tab group (aria-label), for example the workspace's name. A single-panel group is named by its heading.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of every separator between two panels (aria-label).

props.name: fill
props.description: Fill the height the parent gives it (a parent with a definite height, or a flex or grid parent) instead of --pk-dock-height.

slots.name: <panel id>
slots.description: One panel: any element with slot="<id>" (a lowercase id, letters, digits, - and _, up to 40 characters). data-heading is its title (the id when missing) and data-group (left, center, right, bottom) places it in the default arrangement. Panels are slotted, never moved, so a form or a scroll position inside one survives resizing and switching tabs.

slots.name: empty
slots.description: Shown when there is no panel.

slots.name: toolbar-start
slots.description: The start of the toolbar (part toolbar), before the dock's own Panels menu: a place for a host app's own top-level menus (File, Edit, View...). The dock draws none of this; it only gives it a stable spot next to its own controls. The toolbar shows whenever this slot holds something or a panel is closed, and collapses away when both are empty.

events.name: pk-layout-change
events.description: The arrangement changed because of the user or because panels were added or removed: reason is resize (a drag ended or a key moved a separator), activate (a tab was chosen), move (a panel was moved to another group from its Move menu) or panels (the declared panels changed and the layout was repaired). layout is the new document. Not raised for a layout the host set, nor for the first render. Not cancelable.

parts.name: toolbar
parts.description: The bar above the tree: slot toolbar-start (a host app's own menus) then the dock's own Panels menu. Collapses away while both are empty.

parts.name: root
parts.description: The frame that holds the rendered tree.

parts.name: group
parts.description: One tab group or single panel, with its header.

parts.name: header
parts.description: The title bar of a single-panel group.

parts.name: body
parts.description: The scrolling area around a panel's content.

parts.name: status
parts.description: The visually hidden live region that announces a move.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-height
cssProperties.description: Height when fill is not set.

cssProperties.name: --pk-dock-header-height
cssProperties.description: Minimum height of a single-panel header.

a11y: Each separator is a pk-splitter: role=separator with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and its own arrow keys (Left and Right side by side, mirrored in a right-to-left page; Up and Down stacked; Home and End), so every resize has a keyboard path. A group of several panels is a pk-tabs tablist (roving tabindex, arrow keys); a single panel is a labelled section named by its heading. Hidden tab panels are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree. When there is more than one group, its header (or its tab strip, in the trailing slot) carries a Move button (a pk-dropdown, reachable by Tab and opened with Enter or Space) listing every other group: Add as tab in it, or Dock left/right/above/below it; choosing one moves the active panel with dockPanel/moveTab and moves focus to it, and the visually hidden status part announces the result. This is the keyboard and menu alternative to a future pointer drag; nothing here requires a mouse.
mobile: Below 640px a splitter tree cannot show real panels, so the dock draws every open panel in reading order as one tab strip with one panel visible. The layout document is untouched, so widening the window restores the arrangement.
